Q: Logical operators ("and", "or") in Windows batch A:

If you have interested to write an if+AND/OR in one statement, then there is no any of it. But, you can still group if with &&/|| and (/) statements to achieve that you want in one line w/o any additional variables and w/o if-else block duplication (single echo command for TRUE and FALSE code sections):

type nul>nul can be replaced by call;
type 2>nul can be replaced by (call)

Source code
  • std/if_.bat
  • std/if_or.bat
  • std/if_and.bat
  • std/ifn_or.bat
  • std/ifn_and.bat
  • std/if_def.bat
  • std/if_def_and_dir_exist.bat
  • std/if_def_and_file_exist.bat
@echo off
    
setlocal
    
set "A=1" & set "B=2" & call :IF_AND
set "A=1" & set "B=3" & call :IF_AND
set "A=2" & set "B=2" & call :IF_AND
set "A=2" & set "B=3" & call :IF_AND
    
echo.
    
set "A=1" & set "B=2" & call :IF_OR
set "A=1" & set "B=3" & call :IF_OR
set "A=2" & set "B=2" & call :IF_OR
set "A=2" & set "B=3" & call :IF_OR
    
exit /b 0
    
:IF_OR
( ( if %A% EQU 1 ( type nul>nul ) else type 2>nul ) || ( if %B% EQU 2 ( type nul>nul ) else type 2>nul ) || ( echo.FALSE-& type 2>nul ) ) && echo TRUE+
    
exit /b 0
    
:IF_AND
( ( if %A% EQU 1 ( type nul>nul ) else type 2>nul ) && ( if %B% EQU 2 ( type nul>nul ) else type 2>nul ) && echo.TRUE+ ) || echo.FALSE-

    
exit /b 0

More uniform version:

@echo off

setlocal

set "A=1" & set "B=2" & call :IF_AND "%%A%% EQU 1" "%%B%% EQU 2" && echo TRUE+ || echo FALSE-
set "A=1" & set "B=3" & call :IF_AND "%%A%% EQU 1" "%%B%% EQU 2" && echo TRUE+ || echo FALSE-
set "A=2" & set "B=2" & call :IF_AND "%%A%% EQU 1" "%%B%% EQU 2" && echo TRUE+ || echo FALSE-
set "A=2" & set "B=3" & call :IF_AND "%%A%% EQU 1" "%%B%% EQU 2" && echo TRUE+ || echo FALSE-

echo.

set "A=1" & set "B=2" & call :IF_OR "%%A%% EQU 1" "%%B%% EQU 2" && echo TRUE+ || echo FALSE-
set "A=1" & set "B=3" & call :IF_OR "%%A%% EQU 1" "%%B%% EQU 2" && echo TRUE+ || echo FALSE-
set "A=2" & set "B=2" & call :IF_OR "%%A%% EQU 1" "%%B%% EQU 2" && echo TRUE+ || echo FALSE-
set "A=2" & set "B=3" & call :IF_OR "%%A%% EQU 1" "%%B%% EQU 2" && echo TRUE+ || echo FALSE-

exit /b 0

:IF_OR
if %~1 ( exit /b 0 ) else if %~2 ( exit /b 0 ) else exit /b 1
exit /b -1

:IF_AND
if %~1 ( if %~2 ( exit /b 0 ) else exit /b 1 ) else exit /b 1
exit /b -1

or

...

:IF_OR
if %~1 ( exit /b 0 ) else shift
if not "%~1" == "" goto IF_OR
exit /b 255

:IF_AND
if %~1 ( shift ) else exit /b 255
if not "%~1" == "" goto IF_AND
exit /b 0

Output:

TRUE+
FALSE-
FALSE-
FALSE-
    
TRUE+
TRUE+
TRUE+
FALSE-

The trick is in the type command which drops/sets the errorlevel and so handles the way to the next command.

Q: stock management - determine opened state automatically A:

I would combine your medication and medication profiles into one table. That makes sense, because it simplifies your schema and why just having the names in a different table? So, I would have one big medication table containing all the information about all the different medications, that is types of bottles, there are. Something like:

Medication table:

ID Name Class Concentration (mg/ml) Volume (ml) Expires (days)
1 Ciprofloxacin Antibiotic 15 125 5
2 metacam Anti-inflammatory 30 125 365

Next we need to keep track of what comes in stock, is opened, used or removed:

Bottles table:

ID Medication Arrived (date) Opened (date) Expiration (date) Removed (date) Used (ml)
1 2 2024-10-22 2024-10-25 2025-10-25 0000-00-00 56
2 1 2023-11-24 2024-02-11 2024-02-16 2024-03-05 125

So each bottle will be tracked individually. I would advice to use a bar code sticker on the bottle, applied when the bottle is put into stock and which can be scanned every time the bottle is handled. The bar code is directly linked to the ID in this table.

As you can see I have an 'Used' column in the bottles table, this is to track how much content the bottle probably has been used.

I also use an expiration date, to quickly check whether a bottle, that is about to be handled, can still be used. It is computed the moment the bottle is opened.

Finally we need to keep track of usage:

Usage table

ID Bottle ID Patient ID given on Dose (mg) Volume (ml)
1 2 4 2024-01-11 50 7.5
2 1 4 2024-05-13 50 3.5

This is probably all that is needed. The bottles take up a central place in the schema, and each bottle is tracked in detail. The balance of all the bottles can easily be found in the bottles table, so no extra table for that is needed.

This schema can be expanded to account for pill, and other types of medication, as well.

Q: how to make the previous otp code expired in Google2FA used Laravel A:

This is an old question so I hope you solved it for yourself! But I just started using & configuring this package, so I wanted to share.

The 'window' of the OTP code sounds like what you're looking for. But, other settings & notes are available in the package configuration file, so I would recommend checking those out (config/google2fa.php).

Some of the configuration is self-documenting, but there aren't many examples of the use of the window configuration option in the README.

One Time Password Window.

  • Defines how long an OTP will work, or how many cycles it will last. A key has a 30-second cycle.
  • Value of 1 => Keys will be valid for 60 seconds
    • 'window' => 1,
  • So a window of 1 would mean keys from the previous minute and next minute are still valid (approximately always at least 2 previous codes [at 2 codes per minute]).
